lines.text: Apple Pay is finally live in India. But there's a big catch.
Apple rolled it out this week with just one bank partner: Axis Bank.
Only eligible Axis Bank credit cards on Visa or Mastercard work. Tap your iPhone or Apple Watch, or pay online.
The catch? No UPI, and no RuPay cards. And UPI handles most of India's digital payments.
HDFC, ICICI and SBI Card aren't in yet. Reports say Apple wants about 0.2% per payment, and those banks offered less.
Why it matters: iPhone users can finally tap to pay, but Apple Pay starts as a card-only wallet in a UPI-first country.
